text:
Buffalo arrives in Washington on Saturday after a 3-1 home loss to Philadelphia, where Cole Knuble scored his first NHL goal and Dan Vladar stole the game for the Flyers. The Sabres are 2-1-2 in their last five and are playing without Sam Carrick and Matt Grzelcyk, but their record undersells them: a -8 goal difference against a roughly +1 expected one. The Capitals are coming off a 5-2 home loss to the Kings, who erased a two-goal deficit and snapped their own six-game winless run. Washington is 2-3-0 in its last five, without Pierre-Luc Dubois (illness). Dylan Strome has moved beside Tuch and Wilson and is up to 18:46 a night, and Alex Tuch faces Buffalo for the first time since leaving it after 360 games.

The teams are close in chance quality. At five on five, BUF has 53% of the expected goals (a measure of chance quality) and WSH 51%, and our model has it 3.34 to 3.23 for Buffalo. Washington's 4.7 penalties a game keeps feeding opponents power plays. In net, projected starter Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen is at -3.6 goals saved above expected this season but was +9.1 last year. Projected Capitals goalie Charlie Lindgren is at +0.1 this year and -5.9 last year.

Tage Thompson (42% to score) and Tuch (35%) lead the lists. Zach Benson has no goals in ten games despite good chances, so he looks due. Our under-the-radar picks are Josh Norris, whose shots have been dangerous lately, and Noah Ostlund (54% for a point), both as players to watch against a Washington team that gives up chances.
